name: Factory AI
comparable: Samsara / Augury — industrial IoT analytics. But hardware-agnostic and brownfield-ready: works with existing sensors, SCADA, and historians — no proprietary hardware lock-in or rip-and-replace.
whatTheyDo: Sensor-agnostic predictive maintenance and AI-powered CMMS platform for mid-sized manufacturers. Connects to existing sensors, historians, and SCADA systems — no new hardware required. Uses ML to detect anomalies before they cause failures, then tells maintenance teams exactly which component will fail and when. Deploys in under 14 days in brownfield environments. CMMS (work orders, asset management, maintenance scheduling) bundled at no additional cost.
whyFlagged: Information flow pipe between factory floor sensor data and maintenance decision-making. Once Factory AI is embedded in a manufacturer's maintenance workflow — anomaly alerts, work orders, asset monitoring — switching means rebuilding sensor connections across every asset, retraining maintenance teams, and migrating historical data. Hardware-agnostic architecture is the critical differentiator: most competitors require proprietary sensors, creating a high-friction entry but also low exit cost. Factory AI removes the entry barrier and builds the exit barrier through data accumulation and workflow integration. Named customers include Arnott's Group, General Mills, Tip Top, and Darrell Lea — enterprise proof at pre-seed stage. Skalata follow-on is the clearest signal: Skalata's mandate is $500K–$3M ARR companies, confirming real revenue traction.
macroTailwind: Unplanned downtime costs AU industrial businesses median $349,000 per hour (ABB Group data). 69% of AU industrial businesses experience unplanned outages at least monthly. Global predictive maintenance market growing at 30%+ CAGR as OT/IT convergence accelerates. Labour shortages in manufacturing driving demand for AI-assisted maintenance — fewer skilled reliability engineers available, more pressure on software to fill the gap.
needsToBeTrue: Revenue model scales from entry-level $12.5K ARR deals to the $200K ARR expansion potential per customer as more assets are onboarded. US customers (already in the pipeline) convert to meaningful ARR without disproportionate CAC. Skalata backing implies confirmed $500K+ ARR threshold — that number needs to be verified.
risks: Manufacturing enterprise sales are relationship-driven and slow — 3-month sales cycle is already short by industry standards but cash intensity before close is real. Competing against well-funded incumbents (Samsara at $23B market cap, Augury, SparkCognition) with deeper resources. Hardware-agnostic claim needs to hold across the full variety of brownfield plant sensor estates — complexity is underestimated. First-time founders with no prior exit.
founderProfile: Jean-Philippe Picard (CEO) and Tim Cheung (CTO). Tim encountered the predictive maintenance pain directly while working with a UK manufacturer experiencing chronic unplanned downtime — classic problem-first founding. The pair conducted hundreds of conversations with reliability engineers to validate the problem was pervasive before building. Both engaged Antler's residency with deep domain conviction, not a generic AI thesis. Skalata backing provides operator-level mentoring and a bridge to Series A through their portfolio network.
revenueModel: SaaS subscription: $35/user/month (Prevent CMMS, annual billing) + Predict anomaly detection platform (enterprise pricing, undisclosed). Entry contracts ~$12.5K ARR expanding to ~$200K per customer as more assets are onboarded. 0% churn across 15 paying customers. 25% reduction in maintenance costs and 70% reduction in breakdowns reported by customers.
diligence: Confirmed ARR figure — Skalata mandate implies $500K+, but what is the actual number and trajectory?
US customers — how many, what ARR, and what was the go-to-market into North America?
Average deal expansion rate — how many of the 15 customers have grown from $12.5K entry to larger contracts?
Gross margin at current scale — what does the unit economics look like per customer per month?
Hardware-agnostic claim in practice — what is the most complex sensor/historian combination deployed so far?
Competitive displacement: have any deals been won by replacing Samsara or Augury, or is it all greenfield?
Follow-on raise: timing, amount, and who is leading the Series A process?

name: Switchboard
fundingNote: $1.5M AUD pre-seed (Jun 2024) — Archangel, Skalata, Startmate, TEN13, Investible
comparable: SPS Commerce / TrueCommerce — EDI and supply chain integration platforms. AU mid-market equivalent with no entrenched local player at this price point.

founders.name: Hugh Dixson — CEO/Founder (BCG → Uber Ops → Head of M&A, Ofload)

whatTheyDo: Supply chain integration platform connecting businesses to their suppliers, customers, and logistics partners via a single API layer. Automates inventory, order handling, invoicing, and documentation between trading partners — replacing manual processes and fragmented point-to-point integrations. SOC-2 and ISO-27001 certified. Marketed at 10% the cost of existing solutions.
whyFlagged: Pure infrastructure pipe. Once a company's trading partner network (suppliers, customers, 3PLs) is onboarded through Switchboard, switching means re-integrating every partner from scratch. The EDI modernisation play for AU's mid-market — the US incumbents (SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce) are expensive, legacy, and US-focused. Founder lived the problem directly at Ofload, where a manual data entry error cost $100K in a single incident.
macroTailwind: Post-COVID supply chain digitisation pressure; large AU retailers (Woolworths, Coles, Amazon AU) forcing supplier compliance with digital ordering/invoicing; near-shoring driving partner network expansion; AI analytics on supply chain data becoming a boardroom priority.
needsToBeTrue: Signs 3–5 mid-market anchor customers each with multiple trading partners (network effects only kick in with density). The 10% cost claim holds at scale without margin compression. Hugh translates BCG/Ofload pedigree into enterprise sales execution.
risks: Competing against NASDAQ-listed SPS Commerce and IBM Sterling — they have AU distribution. Network effects take time. Pre-seed means limited proof beyond product. Hugh has not previously founded a company — strong operator pedigree but no founder track record.
founderProfile: Hugh Dixson (CEO, sole founder) — BCG, Uber operations, then Head of Operations and Head of M&A at Ofload (one of AU's leading digital road freight platforms). Deep supply chain operations background. The founding insight: a $100K error from manual data entry at Ofload. No prior exit, but operator pedigree is strong and the problem is clearly first-hand.
revenueModel: SaaS subscription — per-integration volume or ARR per trading partner network. Network grows as more partners onboard; revenue per customer increases with usage. High switching cost once supply chain integrations are live.
diligence: How many live paying customers with active trading partner integrations?
Average trading partners per customer — is network density building?
Revenue per customer — what does a typical contract look like?
Gross margin at current scale — does the 10% cost claim leave adequate margin?
Who is closing enterprise deals, and what is the sales cycle length?
Is there an analytics/AI layer planned on top of the integration data?
Any Woolworths or Coles supplier mandate for digital integration that Switchboard benefits from directly?

name: Topograph
fundingNote: €2M seed (Mar 2026) — Seedcamp (lead), Drysdale Ventures, Motier Ventures, Kima Ventures, Better Angle
comparable: Dun & Bradstreet / Kyckr — but source-native, traceable, and real-time. Once compliance workflows integrate directly to official registers via Topograph, switching means re-building country-by-country data pipelines across 40+ jurisdictions.

founders.name: Pierre-Henri Janssens — CEO & Co-Founder (ex-1POINT6 / BNP Paribas)
Hugo Dellinger — CTO & Co-Founder (ex-1POINT6 / BNP Paribas)

whatTheyDo: B2B data infrastructure for global Know-Your-Business (KYB) compliance. Connects directly to official company registers in 40+ countries and delivers real-time, structured business data and supporting documents via a single API endpoint. Every data point is traceable back to its originating official source — not scraped or repackaged. Used by neobanks, PSPs, BNPL providers, and compliance software vendors to automate multi-jurisdiction business identity verification.
whyFlagged: Textbook information flow pipe. Every KYB check — whether for onboarding, ongoing monitoring, or AML — flows through Topograph. The platform doesn't make compliance decisions; it is the data layer that compliance tools and financial institutions run on. Switching means rebuilding country-by-country register integrations across 40+ jurisdictions — a multi-year project for any mid-sized fintech. Seedcamp validation (Revolut, Wise, Pleo alumni) is the strongest European seed signal available. Paying customers already: Hero (neobank), Pledg (BNPL), Lemonway (PSP), Spektr, Dotfile, Ondorse.
macroTailwind: EU AML and KYB regulatory pressure escalating — 6th AML Directive tightening requirements, AI-assisted compliance requiring grounded, verifiable data. Cross-border fintech growth (neobanks, BNPL, PSPs) creating structurally growing demand for multi-jurisdiction business identity infrastructure. Manual country-by-country verification becoming commercially indefensible at scale.
needsToBeTrue: Expansion to 80+ countries (North America, Asia, ME) delivers on the global-coverage thesis without compromising data quality or traceability. Competitor (Kyckr, Bureau van Dijk/Moody's) doesn't out-invest on register integrations. API usage per customer compounds as fintech clients scale their own customer bases.
risks: Capital-intensive to build and maintain register integrations at global scale. Large incumbents (Moody's/Bureau van Dijk, LSEG) could acquire or out-fund. US and Asian expansion earmarked — early on those corridors. Founder pair, not a broader team yet at €2M stage.
founderProfile: Pierre-Henri Janssens (CEO) and Hugo Dellinger (CTO) were both founding team members of 1POINT6, BNP Paribas's embedded payment services subsidiary, where they encountered the KYB data gap directly while onboarding merchants across multiple countries. Classic operator-founders: lived the problem inside a Tier 1 financial institution before building the solution they couldn't find. Prior company building at BNP Paribas scale is the right credential for selling into regulated financial services.
revenueModel: API usage-based pricing — per query / per register data pull. Fintech customers pay per KYB check, with volume discounts. Compliance software vendors pay for platform integration. Revenue scales directly with customer transaction volumes and geographic expansion. Natural NRR expansion as customers grow and enter new markets.
diligence: Current ARR and MRR growth rate — is usage compounding with fintech client growth?
How many active API customers vs total signed up?
Revenue split: direct fintech clients vs compliance software vendor partnerships?
Unit economics per country — does profitability hold as lower-volume jurisdictions are added?
North America and Asia expansion plan — register access complexity and timeline?
Any current or planned relationships with EU regulators or AML authorities that strengthen the moat?
Are Seedcamp terms convertible or priced? Any pro-rata reserved for next round?

name: Fineksi
tagline: AI credit intelligence layer for Indonesian lenders
raised: Accelerating Asia C12 backed — raising (terms TBC)
founders: Wildiyanto Yawin (CEO) — 20+ yrs tech, built tech serving $800M AUM, acquired 2 lending licences
Yuliam Chandra (CTO) — 8+ yrs credit at Indonesia's biggest bank, grew company $0→$1B AUM in 4 years
Yohanes Rico (COO) — 20+ yrs tech solutions, ex-BCA, Modal Rakyat, ex-Fazz Capital Finance
Paramita Wikansari (CCO) — 10+ yrs fintech, 3x built product 0-1-100
thesis: AI credit intelligence infrastructure for SEA lenders. Automates bank statement analysis, document fraud detection, and credit decisioning. Pay-per-page model creates negative churn — ARR grows automatically as customers' loan books grow. Cross-lender data moat: credit patterns across 30+ lenders create proprietary risk signals no single-lender tool can replicate. Path from document extraction layer ($0.10/page) to credit decision engine (Finsight Decision ~1% of loan amount) is the prize. fileAI (graveyarded — $20M raised) validates the document automation market; Fineksi builds deeper into credit decisioning territory fileAI cannot follow.
competitive: Competes with fileAI (horizontal doc automation — graveyarded by us, too expensive), generic credit scoring tools. Differentiation: vertical-only (lenders), outputs a credit decision not just structured data, cross-lender model improves with scale. fileAI cannot make credit decisions without becoming a lender.
contactLog: Neera contacted via Accelerating Asia (Apr 2026). Meeting with Yawin (CEO) scheduled 19 May 2026.
ddQuestions: Business model depth: Finsight Decision at ~1% of loan amount — when does that go live? Any customers already using it? This is the product that makes Fineksi infrastructure, not a tool.
Customer composition: what is the mix of the 30+ customers — P2P lenders, BPR (rural banks), multifinance, commercial banks? How embedded are they in regulated institutions?
Retention quality: is the 99% figure net revenue retention (accounting for expansion) or logo retention? NRR >99% is exceptional; logo retention at $360K ARR is less meaningful.
Cross-lender data moat — is this live today or a vision slide? How many lenders are contributing to the shared model, and can they demonstrate model improvement from cross-lender data?
SC Ventures (finalist Mar 2026): did they proceed to investment/diligence or was it purely a visibility win?
Raise terms: what are they raising, at what valuation, who else is in the round? Is Accelerating Asia leading or a small ticket?
SEA expansion timing: what triggers the Singapore/Philippines/Vietnam expansion — ARR threshold, customer type, or already in motion?
Founder dynamics: Yuliam (CTO) appears to be the strongest credential. Is he fully hands-on or more advisory? How are decisions made across the four founders?
fileAI question: how does Yawin think about fileAI as competitor vs. market validator? What stops fileAI from going deeper into credit decisioning?
notes: Strong 4-person operator team, all with domain depth inside Indonesian lending/banking. Business model is elegant — usage-based pricing aligned with customer success creates negative churn. 99% retention and 20% MoM growth are standout metrics. SC Ventures pitch finalist Mar 2026 (Standard Chartered venture arm, Peak XV, Plug and Play as judges). ISO 27001:2022 certified, penetration tested — important for regulated-entity sales. Deck confidently positions as 'credit infrastructure of APAC' — ambitious but credible given the data moat thesis.
